definition_en: a formal meeting, a period of an activity, a period of study, or a period of use of a computer system
core_image: 长桌旁，人们依次坐下，会议记录翻到新的一页
scene: 委员会在周一召开了一次会议。The committee held a session on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 session 是「会议」（第 1 个义项）；句意：委员会在周一召开了一次会议。

senses.title: Formal meeting
senses.definition: a formal meeting of a group or official body
senses.definitionCN: 团体或官方机构的正式会议
senses.example: The committee held a session on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在周一召开了一次会议。
senses.why: This is the most common formal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的正式义项。

senses.title: Period of activity
senses.definition: a period of time used for one activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项活动的一段时间
senses.example: The band played a long session.
senses.why: An activity can fill a sitting.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动可以占满一次「坐定」的时间。

senses.title: Period of study
senses.definition: a period of study at a school or university
senses.definitionCN: 学校或大学里的一节课、一个学期时段
senses.example: The summer session begins in June.
senses.why: Teaching is organized in sittings.
senses.whyCN: 教学按一个个时段来组织。

senses.title: Computer session
senses.definition: a period of use of a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 使用计算机系统的一段时间
senses.example: Save your work before ending the session.
senses.exampleCN: 结束会话前请保存工作。
senses.why: A login is a modern kind of sitting.
senses.whyCN: 登录是现代的「坐定」形式。

intro.en: Session comes from Latin sessio, a sitting, from sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: session 源自拉丁语 sessio（坐、会期），来自动词 sedere（坐）。

items.en: Sessio meant a sitting or a meeting.
Session kept the sense of a sitting.
items.cn: session 保留了「坐定开会」的含义。

items.en: Session extended to study and computers.
items.cn: session 扩展到学期时段与计算机会话。

note.en: Session is compared with similar-looking words and with words for meetings.
note.cn: 把 session 与形近词以及表示会议的字词作比较。

entries.definition: one of the four parts of the year
the giving up of land or rights

normalIntro.en: Session is a period defined by people sitting down together to do something.
normalIntro.cn: session 是一段由人们坐下来共同做事所定义的时间。

normal.en: The court is now in session.
Each training session lasts an hour.
normal.cn: 每节培训课持续一小时。

normal.en: The band had a late-night session.
normal.cn: 乐队进行了一场深夜演奏。

normal.en: The summer session has three courses.
Log out to close your session.

abstract.en: To sit together is to give a moment a shared shape.
abstract.cn: 坐在一起，就是给一段时间一个共同的形状。

abstract.en: Every meeting is a small stage with a beginning and an end.
abstract.cn: 每一场会议都是有小幕起落的小舞台。

abstract.en: A session ends, but what was decided may keep standing.
abstract.cn: 会期会结束，但作出的决定可能一直立着。

examples.en: The committee held a session on Monday.
examples.cn: 委员会在周一召开了一次会议。

examples.en: The band played a long session.
Save your work before ending the session.
examples.cn: 结束会话前请保存工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: session 源自拉丁语 sedere（坐），核心义「坐下来的一段时间」，引申为会议、会期与会话。

root: 源自拉丁语 sedere（坐）的名词 sessio（坐、会期）。

sensesIntro.en: Session means a formal meeting, a period of activity, a term of study, or a computer login period.
sensesIntro.cn: session 意为正式会议、一场活动、学期时段或计算机会话。

core.en: A period shaped by people sitting together.
core.cn: 由人们坐在一起所形成的一段时间。

branches.cn: 学校或大学的一个学期时段。

branches.en: A period inside a computer system.
branches.cn: 在计算机系统里的一段使用时间。

branches.en: Meeting and activity share a sitting.
branches.cn: 会议与活动都落在一次「坐定」里。

intro.en: Session is built on the Latin root sed-, sit, with the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: session 建立在拉丁词根 sed-（坐）之上，加名词后缀 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin sedere, to sit, also gave sedentary and sediment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）也孕育了 sedentary 与 sediment。

items.example: Sessional work is paid by the hour.

items.meaning: in the middle of a session

definition_zh: 放置；设置；树立；凝固；一套
definition_en: to put something in place, to adjust equipment, to establish something, to become solid, or a group of things used together
core_image: 闹钟被放到床头，指针停在六点
scene: 她把花瓶放在桌上。She set the vase on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 set 是「放置」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把花瓶放在桌上。

senses.title: To place
senses.definition: to put something in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到特定位置
senses.example: She set the vase on the table.
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To adjust
senses.definition: to adjust a device or arrange something in advance
senses.definitionCN: 调整装置或预先安排好
senses.example: He set the alarm for six.
senses.why: Setting a device is placing its state.
senses.whyCN: 设置装置就是安放它的状态。

senses.title: To establish
senses.definition: to establish a record, rule, or example
senses.definitionCN: 创下纪录、定下规则或树立榜样
senses.example: The team set a new record.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍创下了新纪录。
senses.why: An idea can be placed firmly too.
senses.whyCN: 观念也能被牢牢安放。

senses.title: To become solid
senses.definition: to become solid or fixed
senses.definitionCN: 变成固体或固定下来
senses.example: The jelly will set in the fridge.
senses.why: A liquid takes a fixed shape.
senses.whyCN: 液体固定成一种形状。

senses.title: A group of things
senses.definition: a group of things that belong together
senses.definitionCN: 配套的一组东西
senses.example: She bought a set of tools.
senses.why: The noun names things placed together.
senses.whyCN: 名词指被放在一起的一组东西。

intro.en: Set comes from Old English settan, to cause to sit, from the same root as sit.
intro.cn: set 源自古英语 settan（使坐下），与 sit 同根。

items.en: Satjan meant to cause to sit.
Settan meant to place or set.

items.cn: set 保留了放置的含义。

items.en: Set extended to devices and records.
items.cn: set 扩展到装置设置与纪录。

items.en: The noun named a matched group.
items.cn: 名词形式指配套的一组。

note.en: Set is compared with similar-looking words and with words for placing.
note.cn: 把 set 与形近词以及表示放置的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Set is the act of causing something to sit: an object, a clock, a record, or a liquid.
normalIntro.cn: set 就是让某物「坐下」：一个物件、一只钟、一项纪录或一种液体。

normal.en: Set the cup on the shelf.
Set the alarm before bed.
They set a record in the relay.
normal.cn: 他们在接力赛中创下纪录。

normal.en: Leave the cement to set.
This set of dishes has six plates.
normal.cn: 这套餐具共有六个盘子。

abstract.en: To set something is to decide where it belongs.
abstract.cn: 安放某物，就是决定它该在哪里。

abstract.en: A record is a moment set into history.
abstract.cn: 纪录，是被安放进历史的一刻。

abstract.en: Some things set only when we stop holding them.
abstract.cn: 有些东西，只有我们松手后才会定型。

examples.en: She set the vase on the table.
He set the alarm for six.
The jelly will set in the fridge.

dict_mnemonic.text: set 源自古英语 settan（使坐下），核心义「把东西安放到某个位置」，引申出设置、树立、凝固与一套。

root: 源自古英语 settan（使坐下、安放），与 sit 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Set means to place, adjust, establish, become solid, or a matched group.
sensesIntro.cn: set 意为放置、设置、树立、凝固或一套。

core.en: Causing something to take a fixed place.
core.cn: 使某物占据一个固定的位置。

branches.cn: 被放在一起的一组东西。

intro.en: Set is a short native verb that joins with prefixes to make many new words.
intro.cn: set 是简短的日耳曼语本族动词，能与前缀组合出许多新词。

latinIntro.en: Set has no Latin ancestor; Latin ponere, to place, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: set 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 ponere（放置）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She sets the table every night.
The story has a rural setting.
The oven is preset to 180 degrees.
items.exampleCN: 烤箱预设为一百八十度。

items.example: Reset the clock after the power cut.

items.meaning: to balance one effect with another
items.exampleCN: 节省抵消了更高的成本。

items.example: The setter placed the ball well.

definition_en: to live permanently somewhere, to end an argument or problem, to make oneself comfortable, or to sink slowly
core_image: 行李放在新家的地板上，窗外的路终于不再延伸
scene: 他们在一个小镇定居下来。They settled in a small town.
sceneCN: 这里 settle 是「定居」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们在一个小镇定居下来。

senses.title: To live permanently
senses.definition: to go and live permanently in a place
senses.definitionCN: 到某地永久居住下来
senses.example: They settled in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一个小镇定居下来。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代主要义项。

senses.title: To resolve
senses.definition: to end an argument or solve a problem
senses.definitionCN: 结束争论或解决问题
senses.example: The two sides settled the dispute.
senses.why: A matter comes to rest.
senses.whyCN: 事情落定下来。

senses.title: To get comfortable
senses.definition: to make oneself comfortable in a place
senses.definitionCN: 在某处安顿舒服
senses.example: She settled into the chair.
senses.why: The body finds its place.
senses.whyCN: 身体找到自己的位置。

senses.title: To sink down
senses.definition: to sink slowly to the bottom or onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢沉到底部或落在表面
senses.example: The dust settled on the shelf.
senses.why: Even particles come to rest.
senses.whyCN: 连微粒也会落定。

intro.en: Settle comes from Old English setlan, to seat, from setl, a seat.
intro.cn: settle 源自古英语 setlan（使就座），来自 setl（座位）。

items.en: Setlan meant to seat or place.
Settle meant to come to rest.
Settle extended to disputes and debts.
items.cn: settle 扩展到解决争端与清偿债务。

note.en: Settle is compared with similar-looking words and with words for resolving and residing.
note.cn: 把 settle 与形近词以及表示解决和居住的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Settle is the body, the argument, and the dust all finding a place to rest.
normalIntro.cn: settle 是身体、争论与灰尘都找到地方安歇。

normal.en: They settled near the river.
The quarrel was settled quickly.
She settled into a warm chair.
normal.cn: 她在温暖的椅子上安顿下来。

normal.en: Snow settled on the roof.
The bill was settled by card.

abstract.en: To settle is to stop moving long enough to belong.
abstract.cn: 安顿下来，就是停得够久，从而有所归属。

abstract.en: Some arguments end not by winning but by resting.
abstract.cn: 有些争论不是赢出来的，而是停下来才结束的。

abstract.en: Everything heavy eventually finds the ground.
abstract.cn: 沉重之物终会找到地面。

examples.en: They settled in a small town.
examples.cn: 他们在一个小镇定居下来。

examples.en: The two sides settled the dispute.
The dust settled on the shelf.

dict_mnemonic.text: settle 源自古英语 setlan（使就座），核心义「坐下来、安定」，引申出定居、解决与沉降。

root: 源自古英语 setl（座位）与 setlan（使就座），核心义「安放到座位上」。

sensesIntro.en: Settle means to live somewhere, resolve a problem, get comfortable, or sink down.
sensesIntro.cn: settle 意为定居、解决、安顿或沉降。

core.en: Coming to rest in a place or a condition.
core.cn: 在某个位置或状态中安定下来。

branches.en: Home and comfort share one verb.
branches.cn: 安家与安适共用一个动词。

intro.en: Settle grows from the old seat word setl and its suffix -le.
intro.cn: settle 从古老的「座位」词 setl 加后缀 -le 生长而来。

latinIntro.en: Settle has no Latin ancestor; Latin sedere, to sit, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: settle 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 sedere（坐）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The bird settled on the branch.

items.meaning: the act of coming to rest
items.example: The settling of the soil took months.
items.exampleCN: 土壤的沉降花了几个月。

items.example: The first settlers built a bridge.
items.exampleCN: 最早的定居者建了一座桥。

items.example: The family resettled in the north.
items.exampleCN: 这家人重新在北方定居。

definition_zh: 解决；协议；定居点；结算；沉降
definition_en: the ending of an argument, an official agreement, a place where people have settled, the payment of a debt, or the sinking of land
core_image: 几张签好字的纸叠在一起，桌上的争执终于停下
scene: 两国达成了解决方案。The two countries reached a settlement.
sceneCN: 这里 settlement 是「解决」（第 1 个义项）；句意：两国达成了解决方案。

senses.title: Resolution
senses.definition: the ending of an argument or disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 争论或分歧的结束
senses.example: The two countries reached a settlement.
senses.why: This is the core abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的抽象义项。

senses.title: Official agreement
senses.definition: a formal agreement that ends a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 结束争端的正式协议
senses.example: They signed a settlement after talks.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判后他们签署了协议。
senses.why: A resolution is often written down.
senses.whyCN: 解决方案常常被写下来。

senses.title: Place of living
senses.definition: a place where people have made their home
senses.definitionCN: 人们安家落户的地方
senses.example: A small settlement grew by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 河边渐渐形成一个小定居点。
senses.why: People settle, and the place is a settlement.
senses.whyCN: 人们定居下来，这地方就成了定居点。

senses.title: Payment
senses.definition: the payment of a debt or claim
senses.definitionCN: 对债务或索赔的支付
senses.example: The settlement arrived after the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 交易完成后结算款到账了。
senses.why: A debt comes to rest when paid.
senses.whyCN: 债务在付清时落定。

senses.title: Sinking of ground
senses.definition: the slow sinking of land or a building
senses.definitionCN: 土地或建筑物的缓慢下沉
senses.example: The settlement of the ground cracked the wall.
senses.why: The ground also settles.
senses.whyCN: 地面也会落定下沉。

intro.en: Settlement is settle plus -ment, so it names the result of coming to rest.
intro.cn: settlement 由 settle 加 -ment 构成，指「落定」带来的结果。

items.en: Settle meant to come to rest.
Settlement named the paying of a debt.

note.en: Settlement is compared with similar-looking words and with words for agreements and colonies.
note.cn: 把 settlement 与形近词以及表示协议和定居点的词作比较。

entries.definition: a place settled by a group

normalIntro.en: Settlement is what remains after settling: a signed paper, a village, a paid bill, or sunken ground.
normalIntro.cn: settlement 是「落定」之后留下的东西：签好的纸、成形的村庄、付清的账单或下沉的地面。

normal.en: The dispute ended in a settlement.
The peace settlement was signed in May.
A settlement grew around the well.
normal.cn: 一个定居点在井边发展起来。

normal.en: The settlement cleared the debt.
Ground settlement damaged the road.

abstract.en: A settlement is a place where motion becomes a home.
abstract.cn: 定居点，是运动变成家的地方。

abstract.en: Agreement is a bridge built from both sides.
abstract.cn: 协议是从两岸同时修起的一座桥。

abstract.en: Even the ground remembers the weight above it.
abstract.cn: 连地面也记得压在它上面的重量。

examples.en: The two countries reached a settlement.
A small settlement grew by the river.
examples.cn: 河边渐渐形成一个小定居点。

examples.en: The settlement of the ground cracked the wall.

dict_mnemonic.text: settlement 由 settle（安定、解决）加名词后缀 -ment 构成，指解决、协议、定居点或结算。

root: 由 settle（源自古英语 setl，座位）加 -ment 构成，核心义「落定之后的结果」。

sensesIntro.en: Settlement means a resolution, an agreement, a colony, a payment, or the sinking of ground.
sensesIntro.cn: settlement 意为解决、协议、定居点、结算或沉降。

core.en: The state or place that results from settling.
core.cn: 落定之后形成的状态或地方。

branches.en: The written form of that rest.

intro.en: Settlement is settle plus the noun suffix -ment.
intro.cn: settlement 是 settle 加名词后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The base settle is Germanic; Latin sedere, to sit, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 settle 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 sedere（坐）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The settlement was fair to both sides.
items.exampleCN: 这份协议对双方都公平。
海岸边分布着几个定居点。

items.meaning: the act of coming to rest

items.exampleCN: 重新安置计划获得了批准。
未结算的索赔仍未了结。

definition_en: the number 7, a group of seven things, or the age of seven
core_image: 日历上七个方格排成一排，正好是一周
scene: 一周有七天。There are seven days in a week.
sceneCN: 这里 seven 是「七」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一周有七天。

senses.title: The number seven
senses.definition: the number equal to six plus one
senses.definitionCN: 等于六加一的数字
senses.example: There are seven days in a week.
senses.why: This is the basic counting sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的计数义项。

senses.title: A group of seven
senses.definition: a set or group of seven things or people
senses.definitionCN: 由七个事物或人组成的一组
senses.example: The choir sang in sevens.
senses.why: Numbers also name groups.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能命名成组的单位。

senses.title: Age seven
senses.definition: the age of seven years
senses.definitionCN: 七岁的年龄
senses.example: He learned to swim at seven.
senses.why: A number can mark a stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能标记人生的阶段。

intro.en: Seven goes back to Proto-Germanic sebun and further to an ancient root septm.
intro.cn: seven 上溯至原始日耳曼语 sebun，更早来自表示「七」的古老词根 septm。

items.en: Seven also named groups and ages.
items.cn: seven 也用来指成组数量与年龄。

note.en: Seven is compared with similar-looking words and with other number words.
note.cn: 把 seven 与形近词以及其他数词作比较。

entries.definition: more than two but not many

normalIntro.en: Seven fills a week and often carries a sense of completeness.
normalIntro.cn: seven 填满一周，常常带着一种完整感。

normal.en: A week has seven days.
The shop opens at seven.
She has seven brothers.
The seventh day was sunny.
They counted the coins in sevens.
normal.cn: 他们把硬币七个一组地数。

abstract.en: Seven gathers the days into a single week.
abstract.cn: 七，把日子收拢成一个星期。

abstract.en: Some numbers feel complete before we can explain why.
abstract.cn: 有些数字在我们能解释之前，就已显得完整。

abstract.en: Counting is a way of making time visible.
abstract.cn: 计数，是让时间变得可见的一种方式。

examples.en: There are seven days in a week.
He learned to swim at seven.
The choir sang in sevens.

dict_mnemonic.text: seven 来自古英语 seofon，与德语 sieben、拉丁语 septem 同源，核心义就是数字「七」。

root: 源自古英语 seofon（七），与拉丁语 septem 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Seven means the number 7, a group of seven, or the age of seven.
sensesIntro.cn: seven 意为数字七、七个一组或七岁。

core.en: The count that fills a week.
core.cn: 填满一周的那个数。

branches.cn: 由七个事物组成的一组。

branches.en: Number and group share one form.
branches.cn: 数字与成组共用一个形式。

intro.en: Seven is a native Germanic number word that builds a whole family of numbers.
intro.cn: seven 是日耳曼语本族数词，能构成一整族数字词。

latinIntro.en: Seven has no Latin ancestor; Latin septem, seven, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: seven 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 septem（七）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 把纸牌按七张一组分开。

items.example: This is his seventh year here.
items.exampleCN: 这是他在这里的第七年。

items.example: They held a seventieth birthday party.
items.exampleCN: 他们举办了七十岁生日会。

definition_en: the number 17, a group of seventeen things, or the age of seventeen
core_image: 生日蛋糕上插着十七根蜡烛，火苗排成一圈
scene: 班上有十七名学生。There are seventeen students in the class.
sceneCN: 这里 seventeen 是「十七」（第 1 个义项）；句意：班上有十七名学生。

senses.title: The number seventeen
senses.definition: the number equal to sixteen plus one

intro.en: Seventeen is seven plus the old suffix -teen, which means ten more.
intro.cn: seventeen 是 seven 加上古老后缀 -teen（再加十）构成。

items.en: Seventeen also named groups and ages.

note.en: Seventeen is compared with similar-looking words and with other number words.

normalIntro.en: Seventeen is seven with ten more, the age just before adulthood.
normalIntro.cn: seventeen 是七再加十，也是成年之前的那一岁。

normal.en: She is seventeen years old.
Seventeen students passed the test.
normal.cn: 十七名学生通过了考试。

normal.en: We waited seventeen minutes.
He turned seventeen in May.
The seventeenth caller won a prize.
normal.cn: 第十七位来电者获得了奖品。

abstract.en: Seventeen stands at the edge of childhood.
abstract.cn: 十七岁，站在童年的边缘。

abstract.en: A number can hold a whole year of waiting.
abstract.cn: 一个数字，可以装下整整一年的等待。

abstract.en: Counting years is counting changes.
abstract.cn: 数年岁，就是在数变化。

examples.en: There are seventeen students in the class.

scene: 她在比赛中获得第七名。She finished seventh in the race.
sceneCN: 这里 seventh 是「第七」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在比赛中获得第七名。

senses.title: The seventh in order
senses.definition: coming after the sixth in a series
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列中排在第六之后的
senses.example: She finished seventh in the race.
senses.exampleCN: 她在比赛中获得第七名。
senses.why: This is the ordinal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是序数义项。

senses.title: One of seven parts
senses.definition: one of seven equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物被均分为七份中的一份

senses.why: Ordinals also name fractions.

intro.cn: seventh 是 seven 加古老序数后缀 -th 构成。

items.cn: seventhe 形成更清晰的形式。

note.en: Seventh is compared with similar-looking words and with other ordinals.
note.cn: 把 seventh 与形近词以及其他序数词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Seventh marks the place after six and also one slice out of seven.
normalIntro.cn: seventh 既标记六之后的位置，也指七份中的一份。

normal.en: He lives on the seventh floor.
She came seventh in the final.
The seventh day was a holiday.
Only a seventh of the land is farmed.
normal.cn: 只有七分之一的土地被耕种。

normal.en: He is in the seventh grade.

abstract.en: An ordinal turns a count into a position.
abstract.cn: 序数词把数量变成了位置。

abstract.en: Seven parts can make one whole, and one part can still matter.
abstract.cn: 七份能合成一个整体，而一份也仍然重要。

abstract.en: The seventh step is still a step forward.
abstract.cn: 第七步，依然是向前的一步。

examples.en: She finished seventh in the race.
examples.cn: 她在比赛中获得第七名。

examples.en: A seventh of the cake was left.
He lives on the seventh floor.

senses.title: The seventieth in order
senses.definition: coming after the sixty-ninth in a series
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列中排在第六十九之后的
senses.example: The club celebrated its seventieth year.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部庆祝了它的第七十周年。
senses.why: This is the ordinal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是序数义项。

senses.title: One of seventy parts
senses.definition: one of seventy equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物被均分为七十份中的一份
senses.example: A seventieth of the total was set aside.
senses.exampleCN: 总数的七十分之一被留了出来。
senses.why: Ordinals also name fractions.
senses.whyCN: 序数词也能表示分数。

intro.en: Seventieth is seventy plus the ordinal suffix -th.
intro.cn: seventieth 是 seventy 加序数后缀 -th 构成。

items.cn: seventi 形成更清晰的形式。

note.en: Seventieth is compared with similar-looking words and with other ordinals.
note.cn: 把 seventieth 与形近词以及其他序数词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Seventieth is the seventieth position or the seventieth share.
normalIntro.cn: seventieth 既是第七十个位置，也是第七十份份额。

normal.en: They celebrated a seventieth birthday.
normal.cn: 他们庆祝了七十岁生日。

normal.en: The seventieth anniversary drew a crowd.
normal.cn: 七十周年纪念吸引了许多人。

normal.en: He finished seventieth in the marathon.
normal.cn: 他在马拉松中获得第七十名。

normal.en: The seventieth page is blank.

normal.cn: 她拥有这片土地七十分之一的份额。

abstract.cn: 七十年，是用耐心丈量的一生。

abstract.en: An anniversary turns time into a shared object.
abstract.cn: 纪念日把时间变成了可以共享的物件。

abstract.en: Even the smallest share keeps a whole connected.
abstract.cn: 再小的份额，也维系着整体。

definition_en: the number 70, a group of seventy things, or the age of seventy
core_image: 一本旧相册摊开，页码停在第70页

senses.title: The number seventy
senses.definition: the number equal to seven times ten
senses.definitionCN: 等于七乘十的数字

senses.title: A group of seventy

senses.definitionCN: 由七十个事物或人组成的一组
senses.example: Seventy were invited to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 有七十人被邀请参加晚宴。
senses.why: Numbers also name groups.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能命名成组的单位。

senses.title: Age seventy
senses.definition: the age of seventy years
senses.definitionCN: 七十岁的年龄
senses.example: She still paints at seventy.
senses.why: A number can mark a stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能标记人生的阶段。

intro.en: Seventy is seven plus the old suffix -ty, meaning a group of ten.
intro.cn: seventy 是 seven 加古老后缀 -ty（十的倍数）构成。

items.en: Seventy also named groups and ages.

note.en: Seventy is compared with similar-looking words and with other tens.
note.cn: 把 seventy 与形近词以及其他整十数词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Seventy is seven tens, a number often linked to long experience.
normalIntro.cn: seventy 是七个十，常与漫长的经历联系在一起。

normal.en: The old tree is seventy years old.
Seventy people filled the hall.
He is in his seventies.
The temperature reached seventy degrees.
The seventieth guest arrived last.

abstract.en: Seventy years can wear stone into soft curves.
abstract.cn: 七十年，能把石头磨出柔和的曲线。

abstract.en: A lifetime is a number we can only count backward.
abstract.cn: 一生是我们只能倒着数的数字。

abstract.en: Age is a measure, not a limit.
abstract.cn: 年龄是一种尺度，而不是界限。

examples.cn: 这座桥有七十年的历史。

definition_en: more than two but not many, or separate and individual
core_image: 门口站着几个人，彼此隔开一小段距离
scene: 有几个人在外面等候。Several people waited outside.
sceneCN: 这里 several 是「几个」（第 1 个义项）；句意：有几个人在外面等候。

senses.title: More than two but not many
senses.definition: more than two but not a large number
senses.definitionCN: 多于两个但数量不大
senses.example: Several people waited outside.
senses.why: This is the everyday quantity sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的数量义项。

senses.title: Separate and individual
senses.definition: separate or different from one another
senses.definitionCN: 彼此分开或各不相同的
senses.example: They returned to their several homes.
senses.why: The older sense stresses separation.
senses.whyCN: 较早的义项强调彼此分开。

intro.en: Several comes from Anglo-French several, from Medieval Latin separalis, from separ, separate.
intro.cn: several 来自盎格鲁法语 several，上溯至中世纪拉丁语 separalis，源自 separ（分开的）。

items.cn: separ 意为分开的、各别的。

items.en: Separalis meant relating to separate things.
items.cn: separalis 意为与各别事物相关的。
several 意为各别的、不同的。
several 意为分开的或各自的。

items.en: Several came to mean a small number.
items.cn: several 逐渐指不大的数量。

note.en: Several is compared with similar-looking words and with words for an unspecified number.
note.cn: 把 several 与形近词以及表示不确定数量的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Several is a small, separate group of things, more than a couple but not a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: several 是一小群彼此分开的事物，比两三个多，但还算不上人群。

normal.en: Several cars were parked outside.
I have read the book several times.
Several of the windows were open.
They tried several ways to fix it.
normal.cn: 他们试了几种办法来修它。

normal.en: Several years passed before they met again.
normal.cn: 过了几年他们才再次相见。

abstract.en: Several keeps things distinct even while counting them together.
abstract.cn: several 在把事物一起清点的同时，仍让它们彼此分明。

abstract.en: A few is enough to change a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 几个人，就足以改变一个安静的房间。

abstract.en: The exact number matters less than the fact of company.
abstract.cn: 确切的数量，不如有人在场这件事重要。

examples.en: Several people waited outside.
Several of the books were old.
They returned to their several homes.

core.en: A small set of distinct things.

branches.en: The number keeps the items distinct.

items.example: The land is held in severalty.

The severance of the link was final.

definition_en: very strict or harsh, very serious or dangerous, or plain and without decoration
core_image: 暴雨砸在窗上，树枝被风压得几乎折断
scene: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。The storm caused severe damage.
sceneCN: 这里 severe 是「严峻的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。

senses.title: Strict and harsh
senses.definition: very strict or harsh in treatment or judgment
senses.definitionCN: 在对待或评判上非常严格、苛刻的
senses.example: The judge gave a severe warning.
senses.exampleCN: 法官给出了严厉的警告。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义。

senses.title: Very serious
senses.definition: very serious or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 非常严重或危险的
senses.example: The storm caused severe damage.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。
senses.why: Danger is strict in its own way.
senses.whyCN: 危险也有它自己的严厉。

senses.title: Plain and simple
senses.definition: plain and without decoration
senses.definitionCN: 朴素、不加装饰的
senses.example: The room was clean and severe.
senses.why: A severe style allows nothing extra.
senses.whyCN: 朴素的风格不允许任何多余。

intro.en: Severe comes from Latin severus, serious and strict, through Old French.
intro.cn: severe 源自拉丁语 severus（严肃、严格），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Severe extended to serious conditions and plain style.
items.cn: severe 扩展到严峻的状况与朴素的风格。

note.en: Severe is compared with similar-looking words and with words for harshness.
note.cn: 把 severe 与形近词以及表示严厉的词作比较。

entries.definition: more than two but not many

normalIntro.en: Severe is a line drawn hard: strict rules, serious harm, plain style.
normalIntro.cn: severe 是一条画得很硬的线：严格的规则、严重的伤害、朴素的风格。

normal.en: The drought was severe.
He felt severe pain in his back.
The school has severe rules.
The building has a severe design.
The severest winter in years came.
normal.cn: 多年来最严酷的冬天来了。

abstract.en: A severe line cuts away everything unnecessary.
abstract.cn: 严厉的线条，会削去一切多余。

abstract.en: What is serious cannot be softened by ignoring it.
abstract.cn: 严重的事，不能靠忽视来减轻。

abstract.en: Plainness can be a kind of strength.
abstract.cn: 朴素，也可以是一种力量。

examples.en: The storm caused severe damage.
examples.cn: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。

examples.en: The judge gave a severe warning.
examples.cn: 法官给出了严厉的警告。

examples.en: The room was clean and severe.

sensesIntro.en: Severe means strict, very serious, or plain and undecorated.

core.en: A quality that allows no softness or excess.

branches.en: A situation that is very bad.

items.example: This winter is severer than last.
items.exampleCN: 这个冬天比去年更严酷。

items.example: It was the severest test of the year.
items.exampleCN: 这是全年最严峻的考验。

items.example: The severity of the storm surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨的猛烈让我们吃惊。

items.example: The severeness of his tone was clear.

items.exampleCN: 尽管遭遇挫折，她仍坚持不懈。

definition_en: very badly or seriously, in a strict or harsh way, or in a plain and simple way

sensesIntro.en: Shade means a cool dark place, a degree of colour, a lamp cover, or to block light.
sensesIntro.cn: shade 意为阴凉处、色调、灯罩或遮挡光线。

core.en: Light partly blocked, creating rest or tone.
core.cn: 光被部分挡住，产生阴凉或色调。

branches.en: A cool place out of the sun.
The place and the action share a word.
branches.cn: 地方与动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Shade is a native Germanic word that builds shadow and shady.
intro.cn: shade 是日耳曼语本族词，衍生出 shadow 与 shady。

latinIntro.en: Shade has no Latin ancestor; Latin umbra, shadow, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shade 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 umbra（影子）只是语义对应词。

items.example: They ate at a shaded table.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一张有遮阴的桌旁吃饭。

items.example: We rested on a shady bench.
items.exampleCN: 我们在阴凉的长椅上休息。

items.meaning: a dark shape cast by light
items.example: The shadow moved with the sun.
A shadowy figure stood at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 一个朦胧的身影站在门口。
这个消息让聚会黯然失色。

definition_en: a dark shape cast by an object blocking light, a feeling of sadness or threat, a person who follows another, or to follow someone secretly
core_image: 夕阳把人的影子拉得很长，一直伸到街角
scene: 树投下一道长长的影子。The tree cast a long shadow.
sceneCN: 这里 shadow 是「影子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：树投下一道长长的影子。

senses.title: Dark shape
senses.definition: a dark shape made by an object blocking light
senses.definitionCN: 物体挡住光后形成的暗色形状
senses.example: The tree cast a long shadow.
senses.exampleCN: 树投下一道长长的影子。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Mood of threat
senses.definition: a feeling of sadness or danger hanging over something
senses.definitionCN: 笼罩某物的悲伤或危险感
senses.example: The shadow of war hung over the town.
senses.exampleCN: 战争的阴霾笼罩着小镇。
senses.why: A dark shape can also be a mood.
senses.whyCN: 暗色的形状也可以是一种情绪。

senses.title: Secret follower
senses.definition: a person who follows another secretly
senses.definitionCN: 秘密跟随别人的人
senses.example: A shadow followed him through the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 一个跟踪者跟着他穿过街道。
senses.why: A shadow always stays close.
senses.whyCN: 影子总是紧跟不舍。

senses.title: To follow secretly
senses.definition: to follow someone secretly, or to cast a shadow over something
senses.definitionCN: 秘密跟随某人，或给某物投下阴影
senses.example: The detective shadowed the suspect.
senses.why: The noun becomes the verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词。

intro.en: Shadow comes from Old English sceadwe, a form related to shade.
intro.cn: shadow 源自古英语 sceadwe，是与 shade 相关的形式。

items.en: The verb meant to follow or darken.
items.cn: 动词形式意为跟踪或使变暗。

note.en: Shadow is compared with similar-looking words and with words for shade and following.
note.cn: 把 shadow 与形近词以及表示阴影和跟踪的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shadow is the shape that light leaves behind, and anything that follows that closely.
normalIntro.cn: shadow 是光留下的形状，也是任何跟得那么近的东西。

normal.en: His shadow stretched across the road.
The shadow of the mountain covered the village.
She followed him like a shadow.
The detective shadowed the suspect.
There is no shadow of doubt.

abstract.en: A shadow proves that something stands in the light.
abstract.cn: 影子证明有东西站在光里。

abstract.en: What follows us most closely is often our own shape.
abstract.cn: 跟得最近的，常常是我们自己的形状。

abstract.en: Memory can cast a shadow longer than the event.
abstract.cn: 记忆投下的影子，可能比事件本身更长。

examples.en: The tree cast a long shadow.
examples.cn: 树投下一道长长的影子。

examples.en: The shadow of war hung over the town.
examples.cn: 战争的阴霾笼罩着小镇。

examples.en: The detective shadowed the suspect.

root: 源自古英语 sceadwe（影子），与 shade 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shadow means a dark shape, a mood of threat, a secret follower, or to follow secretly.
sensesIntro.cn: shadow 意为影子、阴霾、跟踪者或跟踪。

core.en: The dark shape left where light is blocked.
core.cn: 光被挡住处留下的暗形。

branches.en: A shadow and a follower both stay near.
branches.cn: 影子与跟踪者都留在附近。

intro.en: Shadow is a native Germanic word with a family of adjectives and verbs.
intro.cn: shadow 是日耳曼语本族词，拥有形容词与动词词族。

latinIntro.en: Shadow has no Latin ancestor; Latin umbra, shadow, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shadow 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 umbra（影子）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The path was shadowed by trees.

items.exampleCN: 一个朦胧的身影在等待。

items.example: At noon the wall seemed shadowless.
items.exampleCN: 正午时墙面似乎没有影子。
她的成功让他的黯然失色。

definition_zh: 摇动；动摇；发抖；握手；奶昔
definition_en: to move quickly from side to side, to make someone uncertain, to tremble, to hold hands in greeting, or a thick milk drink
core_image: 瓶子在手中上下晃动，里面的液体撞出细响
scene: 她打开瓶子前摇了摇。She shook the bottle before opening it.
sceneCN: 这里 shake 是「摇动」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她打开瓶子前摇了摇。

senses.title: To move quickly
senses.definition: to move something quickly up and down or side to side
senses.definitionCN: 使某物快速上下或左右移动
senses.example: She shook the bottle before opening it.
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To weaken confidence
senses.definition: to make someone feel uncertain or upset
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到不确定或不安
senses.example: The news shook her confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息动摇了她的信心。
senses.why: A shock can shake the mind.
senses.whyCN: 冲击能摇动内心。

senses.title: To tremble
senses.definition: to tremble with cold, fear, or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷、恐惧或情绪而颤抖
senses.example: He shook with cold.
senses.why: The body shakes when it loses steadiness.
senses.whyCN: 身体失去稳定时就会发抖。

senses.title: To greet with hands
senses.definition: to hold and move someone's hand as a greeting
senses.definitionCN: 以握住并摇动对方的手来表示问候
senses.example: They shook hands at the door.
senses.why: The gesture moves the joined hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个手势让相握的手摇动。

senses.title: Milk drink
senses.definition: a thick drink of milk and ice cream
senses.definitionCN: 由牛奶和冰淇淋摇匀的浓稠饮料
senses.example: He ordered a chocolate shake.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯巧克力奶昔。
senses.why: The drink is shaken before serving.
senses.whyCN: 这种饮料在供应前要摇匀。

intro.en: Shake comes from Old English sceacan, to move with a quick back-and-forth motion.
intro.cn: shake 源自古英语 sceacan，意为快速来回移动。

items.cn: shake 保留了同样的动作。

items.en: Shake named a greeting with hands.
Shake named a thick milk drink.
items.cn: shake 指浓稠的奶制饮料。

note.en: Shake is compared with similar-looking words and with words for trembling and moving.
note.cn: 把 shake 与形近词以及表示颤抖和移动的词作比较。

entries.definition: to move rapidly back and forth

normalIntro.en: Shake moves from the bottle to the voice, the body, the hand, and the glass.
normalIntro.cn: shake 从瓶子一路摇到声音、身体、手和杯子。

normal.en: Shake the juice before drinking.
The bad news shook the whole team.
normal.cn: 坏消息震动了整个团队。

normal.en: She was shaking with fear.
They shook hands and smiled.
He drank a strawberry shake.

abstract.en: To shake is to interrupt steadiness for a moment.
abstract.cn: 摇动，就是短暂地打断稳定。

abstract.en: A handshake can carry more truth than a speech.
abstract.cn: 一次握手，可能比一段话更真实。

abstract.en: What shakes us also shows what holds us.
abstract.cn: 摇动我们的东西，也显出我们被什么托住。

examples.en: She shook the bottle before opening it.
The news shook her confidence.
examples.cn: 这个消息动摇了她的信心。

examples.en: They shook hands at the door.

dict_mnemonic.text: shake 源自古英语 sceacan（摇动），核心义「来回快速移动」，引申出动摇、发抖与握手。

root: 源自古英语 sceacan（摇动），与德语 schütteln 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shake means to move quickly, to weaken confidence, to tremble, to greet with hands, or a milk drink.
sensesIntro.cn: shake 意为摇动、动摇、发抖、握手或奶昔。

core.en: A quick back-and-forth movement.
core.cn: 快速的来回移动。

branches.en: A body that cannot stay still.

intro.en: Shake is a strong native verb with irregular past forms.
intro.cn: shake 是日耳曼语本族强变化动词，过去式不规则。

latinIntro.en: Shake has no Latin ancestor; Latin quatere, to shake, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shake 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 quatere（摇动）只是语义对应词。

items.example: He was shaken by the news.
She filled the shaker with ice.

items.exampleCN: 有力的握手能建立信任。

definition_en: used with I or we for the future, used in rules to mean must, or used to make an offer or suggestion
core_image: 电话听筒贴在耳边，明天的那通电话还没有拨出
scene: 我明天会给你打电话。I shall call you tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 shall 是「将」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我明天会给你打电话。

senses.title: Future with I or we
senses.definition: used with I or we to talk about the future
senses.definitionCN: 与 I 或 we 连用，表示将来
senses.example: I shall call you tomorrow.
senses.why: This is the traditional future use.
senses.whyCN: 这是传统的将来时用法。

senses.title: Must in rules
senses.definition: used in official rules to mean must
senses.definitionCN: 在正式规定中表示「必须」
senses.example: Students shall not smoke on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 学生不得在校园内吸烟。
senses.why: Law and rules use shall for obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法律与规章用 shall 表示义务。

senses.title: Offer or suggestion
senses.definition: used in questions to offer something or suggest an action
senses.definitionCN: 在疑问句中用于提供某物或建议行动
senses.example: Shall we go for a walk?
senses.why: The question asks for agreement.
senses.whyCN: 这种疑问句在征求同意。

intro.en: Shall comes from Old English sceal, meaning owe or must, and softened into a future marker.
intro.cn: shall 源自古英语 sceal（欠、必须），后来弱化为将来时的标记。

items.en: Skal meant I owe or I must.
items.cn: skal 意为「我欠」或「我必须」。
shall 同时标记义务与将来。

items.en: Shall became a future helper with I and we.
items.cn: shall 成为与 I、we 连用的将来助动词。
规章保留了 shall 的义务含义。

note.en: Shall is compared with similar-looking words and with other modal verbs.
note.cn: 把 shall 与形近词以及其他情态动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shall began as a word for owing and became a gentle way to mark the future or a rule.
normalIntro.cn: shall 最初表示「欠」，后来变成标记将来或规定的温和方式。

normal.en: I shall see you next week.
We shall need more time.
The rule says visitors shall sign in.
Shall I open the window?
Shall we begin?

abstract.en: A word of obligation can soften into a word of invitation.
abstract.cn: 一个表示义务的词，也能软化成邀请。

abstract.en: The future is often spoken as a promise.
abstract.cn: 将来，常常是被当作承诺说出来的。

abstract.en: Rules sound gentler when they use an old, quiet word.
abstract.cn: 用上一个古老而安静的词，规定也会显得温和。

examples.en: I shall call you tomorrow.
Students shall not smoke on campus.
examples.cn: 学生不得在校园内吸烟。

examples.en: Shall we go for a walk?

dict_mnemonic.text: shall 源自古英语 sceal（必须、应当），后来成为表示将来、规定与提议的情态动词。

root: 源自古英语 sceal（欠、必须），与 should 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shall marks the future with I or we, obligation in rules, or a polite offer.
sensesIntro.cn: shall 表示与 I、we 连用的将来、规章中的义务或礼貌的提议。

core.en: A modal word that moves from owing to intending.
core.cn: 从「欠」走向「打算」的情态词。

branches.en: A future spoken with I or we.
branches.cn: 与 I 或 we 连用的将来。

branches.en: A question that offers or suggests.
Promise and duty share one form.
branches.cn: 承诺与义务共用一个形式。

branches.en: The same word can command or invite.
branches.cn: 同一个词既能命令，也能邀请。

intro.en: Shall belongs to the old Germanic modal verbs, with should as its past form.
intro.cn: shall 属于古老的日耳曼语情态动词，should 是它的过去式形式。

latinIntro.en: Shall has no Latin ancestor; Latin debere, to owe, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shall 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 debere（欠、应当）只是语义对应词。
